_comment: Curated list of extensions for the Atlantic store page. Packages are
downloaded from addons.mozilla.org by slug; nothing is mirrored here.
'expected' is a compatibility verdict derived from the add-on's declared
permissions using the same rule WebExtensionStore::verdictFor() applies to
search results, then reviewed by hand. 'verified' means somebody actually
ran it on a device — set it to true only after doing so, per extension.
The catalog is a recommendation, never a restriction: the store page can
search all of AMO and will install anything the user asks for, including

extensions.name: Dark Reader
extensions.note: Dimming is a content script; its context-menu entries work too now that browser.contextMenus is supported.

extensions.name: Unpaywall
extensions.summary: Finds free, legal copies of paywalled research papers.

extensions.name: YouTube NonStop
extensions.summary: Dismisses YouTube's "are you still watching?" prompt.
extensions.note: A single content script; nothing else.

extensions.name: Enhancer for YouTube
extensions.summary: Playback speed, volume, quality and layout controls for YouTube.
extensions.note: Content script plus settings in storage — no APIs Atlantic withholds.

extensions.name: Terms of Service; Didn't Read
extensions.summary: Grades and summarises the terms of the site you are on.

extensions.name: Simple Translate
extensions.note: Selection translation and its context-menu entry should both work.

extensions.name: Read Aloud
extensions.note: Start it from the popup or its context-menu entry.

extensions.name: Tranquility Reader
extensions.summary: Strips a page down to its readable content.
extensions.note: Strips the page from its context-menu entry or the popup.

extensions.name: Image Search Options
extensions.summary: Reverse image search from the page.
extensions.note: Driven entirely from the context menu, which Atlantic now shows on a long press.

extensions.name: SponsorBlock
extensions.summary: Skips sponsored segments in YouTube videos.
extensions.note: Skipping is a content script; the parts that inject scripts dynamically work now that browser.scripting is supported.

extensions.name: uBlock Origin
extensions.note: Listed so the answer is easy to find: uBlock Origin blocks through webRequest, which Atlantic does not provide, so it will install and then do nothing. Atlantic's built-in blocker already runs the same filter lists through the Brave engine — turn it on in Settings instead.
